subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a new `gateway.peers` cross-gateway session-routing surface now, or hold this work until the broader gateway federation trust contract is defined?
rationale: The requested behavior is useful and missing, but this PR changes Gateway trust boundaries, URL routing policy, session-state ownership, and message-delivery semantics in ways automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Hold for secure federation contract
options.body: Define peer identity, approved URL policy, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session visibility before merging any core cross-gateway session routing.

options.title: Narrow to existing remote contract
options.body: Drop raw arbitrary peer URLs and prove a smaller implementation that only uses the existing `gateway.remote.url`/allowlist path with focused compatibility tests.

options.title: Route to plugin or bridge
options.body: Keep core gateway-local for now and ask for a plugin/MCP bridge or missing extension API instead of a bundled core surface.

recommendation.title: Hold for secure federation contract
recommendation.body: Define peer identity, approved URL policy, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session visibility before merging any core cross-gateway session routing.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for the session-tool owner boundary and gatewayUrl security policy points to this owner candidate.
